dedupe_keys.name: impacts of agrisolar co location on the food energy water nexus in the california central valley nature sustainability 2025

description: This case study analyses the food, energy, water and economic effects of converting farmland to solar photovoltaic arrays, called agrisolar co-location, for 925 arrays totalling 2.53 GWp over 3,930 hectares in California's Central Valley. It estimates the crop output and calories displaced, the irrigation water no longer pumped and the change in farm cash flow. It was written by Jacob Stid, Siddharth Shukla, Anthony Kendall, Annick Anctil, David Hyndman, Jeremy Rapp and Robert Anex and published in Nature Sustainability on 21 April 2025. Coverage is the Central Valley, a region with high irrigation pumping costs. The article is free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, the datasets and outputs are publicly available on Zenodo, and the FEWLS analysis code is on GitHub and Zenodo. Findings: co-location displaces food production but raises farmers' economic security and water sustainability, and converting feed, silage and biofuel cropland offsets much irrigation water with little loss of calories. Caveats: the solar area counted excludes other solar infrastructure, and market responses elsewhere are not modelled. For simulation it gives a reusable tool and data for weighing land conversion from agriculture to energy in capacity planning and drought adaptation. It is related to the WRI agricultural exposure to water stress record in this catalogue. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 (article); Zenodo archive CC-BY-4.0 and MIT; code MIT.
